memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"Aaron and his sons shall eat the rest of it, but it is to be eaten without yeast in the sanctuary area; they are to eat it in the courtyard of the tent of meeting."'" - Lev 6:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The priests ate their portion, but not wherever they liked. Not at home, not on the road. In the courtyard of the tent of meeting.

Their food came from God's altar, and it was eaten in God's presence.

There is a quiet beauty in this. The priests' daily bread and their daily nearness to God were the same event. They could not separate provision from presence, because God had joined them together.

Most of us eat without thinking. But the pattern here suggests something worth recovering: receiving our provision consciously in God's presence, aware of where it came from.

That is part of why Christians say grace before meals — not as a superstition or a formality, but as a small daily act of remembering. This came from God, and I am eating it before Him.

Jesus taught us to pray, Give us today our daily bread (Mtt 6:11). He also said, Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God (Mtt 4:4).

Whatever is on your table today came from His altar. Eat it in His courtyard.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I receive my daily provision consciously from God, or automatically?
2. What would it look like to bring more of my ordinary life into God's presence?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the food on my table and the provision in my life. Help me to receive it in Your presence rather than out of habit. Amen.
